title: Michimalonco's Mapuche warriors attack the new city of Santiago
description: As toqui of the Mapuches, Michimalonco led an assault on Santiago del Nuevo Extremo to free chiefs held by the Spaniards. Defended by Inés de Suárez while Pedro de Valdivia was away, the town was almost all destroyed before the attackers were driven off.

skip: The lead gives only the place and dates of the convention; it cannot carry two sentences.

title: A Hospitaller gunpowder factory explodes in Valletta
description: A Hospitaller gunpowder factory in Valletta, Malta, blew up by accident, killing 22 people and badly damaging a number of buildings. It stood in the lower part of the city, near the Slaves' Prison, and had replaced an earlier one in Fort St. Angelo.

title: Castilian forces occupy Gibraltar after the first siege
description: Ferdinand IV's army occupied Gibraltar after its Muslim defenders surrendered to the forces of Juan Núñez de Lara and Alonso Pérez de Guzmán, who let some 1,125 inhabitants leave unharmed. Muslim forces retook the town in the third siege of Gibraltar in 1333.

title: Ögedei is proclaimed Khan of the Mongols at the Kherlen kurultai
description: After ritually declining three times, Ögedei, whom Genghis Khan had wished to succeed him, was proclaimed Khan at the kurultai of Khödöö Aral on the Kherlen River. His younger brother Tolui had held the regency since Genghis Khan's death in 1227.

title: Congress sets the dates for the first US presidential election
description: The Confederation Congress fixed 7 January 1789 for choosing the electors, 4 February for their vote for president and 4 March for the Constitution to take effect, with New York City as the temporary capital. It formed a quorum for the last time on 10 October.

title: French and American forces begin the siege of Savannah
description: A joint Franco-American force set out to retake Savannah, Georgia, captured the year before by a British expeditionary corps under Lieutenant-Colonel Archibald Campbell. The siege, also called the second battle of Savannah, lasted until 18 October 1779.

title: Robert College opens in Bebek with 31 students
description: Founded by the American philanthropist Christopher Robert and the missionary Cyrus Hamlin, Robert College opened with 31 students at Bebek Seminary School in Istanbul. It is the oldest continuously operating American school outside the United States.

title: Richard Montgomery's Americans lay siege to Fort St. Jean
description: American Brigadier General Richard Montgomery besieged the town and fort of Saint-Jean in the British province of Quebec, opening the Continental Army's invasion of Quebec. The fort fell on 3 November, and Montgomery went on to take Montreal.

title: The United States and the Lenape sign the Treaty of Fort Pitt
description: Signed at Fort Pitt, Pennsylvania, now the site of Downtown Pittsburgh, it was the first formal treaty between the United States and any Native American group. It was essentially a treaty of military alliance between the Lenape Nation and the United States.

title: The Battle of Chickamauga opens between Union and Confederate forces
description: The three-day battle ended a Union offensive in southeastern Tennessee and northwestern Georgia. It was the first major battle of the war in Georgia, the most significant Union defeat in the Western Theater, and second only to Gettysburg in casualties.

title: John Bell Hood opens the Franklin–Nashville campaign
description: The Confederate general John Bell Hood began a series of battles in Alabama, Tennessee and northwestern Georgia, also known as Hood's Tennessee campaign. It failed in its aim of drawing William Tecumseh Sherman back out of Georgia and lasted until 27 December.

title: Rosecrans halts Sterling Price's advance at the Battle of Iuka
description: At Iuka, Mississippi, Union Brigadier General William S. Rosecrans stopped the advance of the Confederate Army of the West under Major General Sterling Price. It was the opening battle of the Iuka–Corinth Campaign of the American Civil War.

title: Sheridan defeats Jubal Early at the Third Battle of Winchester
description: Near Winchester, Virginia, Union Major General Philip Sheridan defeated Lieutenant General Jubal Early in one of the largest and bloodiest battles in the Shenandoah Valley. The Union counted some 5,000 casualties, the Confederates about 4,000 of 15,500.

title: The Meiō earthquake and tsunami strike the coast of Japan
description: An estimated magnitude 8.6 earthquake off Nankaidō set off a tsunami, with reported deaths ranging from 5,000 to 41,000. It washed away the building that housed the Great Buddha at Kōtoku-in in Kamakura; the statue survived and has stood outside ever since.

title: Babington and Ballard are executed for the plot against Elizabeth I
description: Anthony Babington, John Ballard and the other men tried with them were hanged, drawn and quartered for plotting to kill Elizabeth I and put Mary, Queen of Scots, on the throne. The outcry led Elizabeth to let the next group hang until dead first.

title: The Ever Victorious Army wins at Cixi but loses its commander
description: The Qing dynasty's European-trained Ever Victorious Army defeated Taiping forces at Cixi, but its commander, the American mercenary Frederick Townsend Ward, was mortally wounded. His death began a period of decline for the force under Henry Andres Burgevine.

title: Empress Dowager Cixi seizes power and ends the Hundred Days' Reform
description: Cixi's seizure of power ended a reform movement begun on 11 June that had sought to modernise China's institutions after its defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War. Though brief, it inspired many of the New Policies reforms launched after 1901.

title: Paraguay repulses the allied assault at Curupayty
description: About 20,000 Brazilian, Argentine and Uruguayan troops attacked trenches at Curupayty held by 5,000 Paraguayans and 49 cannons under José Eduvigis Díaz. The Brazilian navy's fire failed them, and it was Paraguay's only significant victory of the war.

title: A Spanish force fights its way past an ambush at Zutphen
description: Led by the Marquis del Vasto, a Spanish force broke through an English and Dutch ambush near Warnsveld and Zutphen, which the Earl of Leicester was besieging. Leicester had been sent with an English army after England entered the war against Spain in 1585.

title: The Eastern Mongols defeat a Ming army on the Kherlen River
description: The battle between the Eastern Mongols and the Ming dynasty was fought on the banks of the Kherlen River on the Mongolian Plateau. It was the second significant victory over Ming China by the Mongols since 1368.

title: Ras Alula's Ethiopian army defeats the Mahdists at Kufit
description: Ethiopian forces under Ras Alula defeated the Mahdist Sudanese of Osman Digna at Kufit after two days of fighting. It steadied the Sudanese-Ethiopian border, though Mahdist raids went on until 1889 and Italy used the fighting to found a colony in Eritrea.

title: Saigō Takamori's samurai fall at the Battle of Shiroyama
description: In Kagoshima, the heavily outnumbered samurai of Saigō Takamori made a last stand against Imperial Japanese Army troops under Yamagata Aritomo and were annihilated. The battle ended the Satsuma Rebellion, the last internal mutiny in the Empire of Japan.

title: Ragenfrid defeats Theudoald at the Battle of Compiègne
description: Ragenfrid defeated Theudoald at Compiègne in the first definite battle of the civil war among the Franks. The war had broken out after the death of Pepin of Heristal, Duke of the Franks, on 16 December 714.

title: The Frisians defeat Count William IV of Holland at Staveren
description: At the Battle of Staveren, also called the Battle of Warns, the Frisians repelled the Hollanders of Count William IV from the eastern coast of the Zuiderzee. Its annual commemoration is important for many Frisian nationalists.

title: A Polish–Lithuanian relief force defeats the Swedes at Kircholm
description: Near Kircholm, now Salaspils in Latvia, a smaller relief force of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth defeated a Swedish expedition besieging Riga, and the Swedes abandoned the attempt. The battle was part of the Polish–Swedish War of 1600–1611.

skip: A single rail crash (the Old 97 mail train); trivial for a history site.

title: Pope Pontian resigns and is exiled to the mines of Sardinia
description: Arrested during the persecution of Christians in the reign of the Emperor Maximinus Thrax, Pontian, bishop of Rome since 21 July 230, resigned his office. He was exiled to the mines of Sardinia together with the Christian writer Hippolytus of Rome.

title: Constantius II defeats the usurper Magnentius at Mursa
description: At Mursa, near the Via Militaris in the province of Pannonia, the eastern Roman armies of Emperor Constantius II defeated the western forces of the usurper Magnentius. One of the bloodiest battles in Roman history, it was a pyrrhic victory for Constantius.

title: Leo I, later called Leo the Great, becomes Bishop of Rome
description: Leo was consecrated as Bishop of Rome after the death of Sixtus III on 18 August 440. He held the office for more than twenty years, until his death on 10 November 461, and came to be known as Leo the Great.

title: An earthquake ruins much of Antigua Guatemala
description: An earthquake of an estimated magnitude of 7.4 destroyed much of the architecture of Antigua Guatemala, then the colonial capital of Central America, ruining over 3,000 buildings. The authorities considered moving the seat of government to a safer place.

title: The Lebanese Council opens to reform the Maronite Church
description: Maronite and Latin clergy under Yusuf ibn Siman as-Simani met at the monastery of Our Lady of Luwayza near Zouk Mosbeh to address the church's dependency on the aristocracy and the patriarchs' rights. Its decrees took several decades to carry out.

title: Cardinal bishops alone elect Pope Alexander II
description: Under Nicholas II's bull In Nomine Domini, the cardinal bishops were the sole electors of a pope for the first time, choosing Anselm of Baggio, Bishop of Lucca. Opposition to the election forced his coronation into San Pietro in Vincoli, not St. Peter's.

title: John XIII becomes pope amid Otto I's conflict with Roman nobles
description: John XIII's pontificate was caught up in the conflict between the Holy Roman emperor Otto I and the Roman nobility. He arranged a Byzantine marriage for Otto II to support the Ottonian imperial claim, and set up the church hierarchy in Poland and Bohemia.

title: Michael I Rangabe is proclaimed Byzantine emperor
description: A courtier of Nikephoros I who had survived the disastrous campaign against the Bulgars, Michael was preferred over the severely injured Staurakios and proclaimed emperor by Patriarch Nicephorus I. Staurakios was forced to give up his claim.

title: Confederates repulse a Union attack at Saltville, Virginia
description: Confederate forces defeated a Union attack near the town of Saltville, Virginia, in the First Battle of Saltville. A massacre of wounded Union prisoners followed, and the battle is also known as the Saltville Massacre.

title: Muhammad VII becomes the twelfth Nasrid ruler of Granada
description: Muhammad VII, son of Yusuf II and grandson of Muhammad V, came to the throne of the Emirate of Granada on his father's death. In 1394 he defeated an invasion by the Order of Alcántara, then restored peace with Henry III of Castile.

title: Earl Van Dorn attacks Rosecrans at the Second Battle of Corinth
description: Confederate forces under Earl Van Dorn attacked the Union defences around Corinth, Mississippi, in a battle that lasted two days. For the second time in the Iuka–Corinth Campaign, William S. Rosecrans defeated a Confederate army.

title: Mexico adopts its first constitution as a federal republic
description: The Federal Constitution of the United Mexican States, the first constitution of Mexico, was enacted and made the country a federal republic. It inaugurated the First Mexican Republic.

title: Louis XI signs the Treaty of Conflans with Charles of Charolais
description: King Louis XI of France was forced to sign the treaty with Count Charles of Charolais. It came months after the Battle of Montlhéry, where the French dukes of Alençon, Burgundy, Berry, Bourbon and Lorraine had fought the king to a standstill.

title: Formosus is elected pope after the death of Stephen V
description: Formosus's reign was troubled by power struggles over Constantinople, West Francia and the Holy Roman Empire, in which he sided with Arnulf of Carinthia against Lambert of Spoleto. After his death his remains were exhumed and put on trial in the Cadaver Synod.

title: Venice defeats Boucicaut's Genoese fleet off Modon
description: The fleet of the Republic of Venice decisively defeated that of the Republic of Genoa, then under French control and commanded by the French marshal Jean Le Maingre, known as Boucicaut. It was one of the last clashes of the Venetian–Genoese wars.

title: The Battle of Perryville halts the Confederate invasion of Kentucky
description: West of Perryville, Kentucky, Braxton Bragg's Confederate Army of Mississippi won a tactical victory over part of Don Carlos Buell's Union Army of the Ohio, but then withdrew to Tennessee. The Union kept control of Kentucky for the rest of the war.

title: The cutter Eagle's crew fights the Royal Navy off Long Island
description: Beached on Long Island, the Revenue Marine's cutter Eagle fought on, her crew firing at Royal Navy ships from shore with cannon recovered from her. After three days they ran out of ammunition and the British towed her off; no one was killed on either side.

title: Henry of Guise defeats a Huguenot-recruited army at Dormans
description: In the fifth War of Religion in France, the army of Henry I, Duke of Guise, defeated the German army recruited by the Huguenots under John Casimir of the Palatinate-Simmern. Among the Protestants captured was the writer Philippe de Mornay.

title: The Continental Congress founds the Continental Navy
description: The Continental Congress founded a navy to fight British forces in the American Revolutionary War, and in 1776 Commodore Esek Hopkins was given its command. It never matched the Continental Army's successes but was the predecessor of the United States Navy.

title: Warren's II Corps repels A. P. Hill at Bristoe Station
description: At Bristoe Station, Virginia, the Union II Corps under Gouverneur K. Warren surprised and repelled Lieutenant General A. P. Hill's attack on the Union rearguard. The Confederates failed to drive the Union army out of Virginia.

title: Ottoman attacks fail at Żurawno and peace talks begin
description: Superior Ottoman forces failed to break through the Polish defences under Jan Sobieski at Żurawno, where fighting had gone on since 25 September, and the Ottoman commander opened negotiations. The Treaty of Żurawno was signed in the aftermath.

title: Confederates capture the Union garrison at Glasgow, Missouri
description: During Price's Missouri Expedition, the Union garrison of Glasgow, Missouri, surrendered to Confederate forces. The capture gave them needed weapons and lifted Confederate morale, which had been dented by the defeat at the Battle of Pilot Knob.

title: Patriot cavalry rout Loyalists at Raft Swamp, North Carolina
description: Patriot cavalry under Major Joseph Graham broke the Loyalist horsemen of Colonel Hector McNeill near Red Springs, and the Loyalists scattered at nightfall. It was the last battle fought in North Carolina, four days before the British surrender at Yorktown.

title: Otto I defeats the Obotrites in the Battle on the Raxa
description: Otto I of Germany and his Rani allies defeated the Obotrite federation under Nako and his brother Stoigniew in a fight for the Billung march. Coming after his August victory over the Magyars at the Lechfeld, it marked the high point of Otto's reign.

skip: A weather record (the earliest reported tornado in England, its strength estimated from reports written 30 years later); trivial for a history site.

title: Riots against Aleppo's Christians begin, ending in a massacre
description: Muslim residents, largely from the eastern quarters of Aleppo, attacked Christian residents of the northern suburbs of Judayde and Salibeh in two days of rioting. Numerous people were killed, among them Peter VII Jarweh, the Syriac Catholic Patriarch.

title: Adeodatus I is consecrated pope after imperial approval
description: Adeodatus I, also called Deusdedit, was the first priest elected pope since John II in 533, in a period when popes needed the Byzantine emperor's approval to be consecrated. The first use of lead seals, or bullae, on papal documents is attributed to him.

title: Sheridan rallies to defeat Early at the Battle of Cedar Creek
description: Jubal Early's Confederates took over 1,000 prisoners and 20 guns in a morning attack in the Shenandoah Valley, but Philip Sheridan's Union army rallied in the afternoon and drove them away. The battle ended the last Confederate threat to Washington.

title: Peru and Chile sign the Treaty of Ancón
description: Signed at Ancón, near Lima, the treaty settled the two nations' remaining territorial differences as Peru's part in the War of the Pacific came to an end. By its terms Peru ceded the province of Tarapacá to Chile.

title: Chile and Bolivia sign the Treaty of Peace and Friendship
description: Signed in Santiago de Chile twenty years after the end of the War of the Pacific, the treaty set the boundary between the two countries through 96 points from Cerro Zapaleri to Cerro Chipe. It also regulated relations between them.

title: Go-Kameyama abdicates, ending Japan's Southern Court
description: Emperor Go-Kameyama, the 99th emperor in the traditional order of succession and the last of the Southern Court, gave up the throne to his rival Go-Komatsu. Go-Komatsu, the sixth and last emperor of the Northern Court, counts as the 100th emperor.

skip: The article only gives the computed astronomy of the eclipse; the story of its record in China and the executed astronomers rests on the On this day line alone.

title: Fort Mercer's defenders repulse a Hessian attack at Red Bank
description: A force of 1,200 Hessian troops sent to take Fort Mercer, on the New Jersey bank of the Delaware River, was defeated by a smaller Continental Army force. Thaddeus Kosciuszko had built the fort that year to block the British advance on Philadelphia.

title: Scotland defeats England at the Battle of Sark
description: Also called the Battle of Lochmaben Stone and dated to 23 October 1448 or 1449, it was the first decisive Scottish victory over England since the Battle of Otterburn in 1388. It was the last pitched battle between the two kingdoms in the medieval period.

title: Union forces defeat Sterling Price at the Battle of Westport
description: In what is now Kansas City, Missouri, Union troops under Samuel R. Curtis decisively defeated the outnumbered Confederates of Sterling Price, with more than 30,000 men engaged. It ended the last major Confederate offensive west of the Mississippi River.

title: A mob kills Chinese residents in the Los Angeles massacre
description: About 500 white and Latino Americans attacked, robbed and murdered Chinese residents of Calle de los Negros, in today's old Chinatown; an estimated 17 to 22 were lynched. The mob formed after a policeman and a rancher died in a clash of rival tongs.

title: The Shinpūren rebellion breaks out against the Meiji government
description: Opposed to the Westernisation of Meiji Japan and the end of the Tokugawa feudal hierarchy, the Keishintō, extremist Shinto former samurai, made a surprise attack on the government in Kumamoto. Former samurai had become a class without special privileges.

title: Hawke's fleet defeats the French off Cape Finisterre
description: A British fleet of fourteen ships of the line under Rear-Admiral Edward Hawke intercepted a French convoy of 250 merchant ships bound for the West Indies and its escort of eight ships of the line under Henri-François des Herbiers, and defeated the French.

title: Yi Sun-sin holds the Myeongnyang Strait with 13 ships
description: With only 13 ships left after the defeat at Chilcheollyang, Admiral Yi Sun-sin of the Joseon Navy routed a Japanese fleet of 300 ships near Jindo Island. The Japanese had been sailing to support their army's advance toward the Joseon capital, Hanyang.

title: The First Continental Congress adjourns in Philadelphia
description: Delegates of twelve of the Thirteen Colonies had met at Carpenters' Hall since 5 September. They had gathered after the British blockaded Boston Harbor and Parliament passed the Intolerable Acts in answer to the Boston Tea Party.

title: Honorius I is consecrated pope after the death of Boniface V
description: Honorius I was consecrated as bishop of Rome two days after the death of Boniface V, who had done much for the Christianisation of Anglo-Saxon England. Honorius held the office until his death on 12 October 638.

title: Missouri's governor issues the Extermination Order against Mormons
description: Governor Lilburn Boggs issued Missouri Executive Order 44, ordering all Mormons to leave the state or be killed, after the Battle of Crooked River. That clash began when Ray County militia seized Mormon hostages and Mormons tried to free them.

title: The Ottomans break the Mamluk cavalry at Yaunis Khan
description: Mamluk cavalry under Janbirdi al-Ghazali attacked the Ottomans of Grand Vizier Hadım Sinan Pasha as they crossed Gaza on their way to Egypt, but the charge was broken. The wounded al-Ghazali and his remaining forces retreated to Cairo.

title: Adal forces of Imam Ahmad fight Dawit II at Amba Sel
description: The forces of Imam Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi of the Adal Sultanate fought the Ethiopians under Emperor Dawit II at Amba Sel, and Adal seized southern Ethiopia. The war between the Christian Ethiopian Empire and Muslim Adal lasted from 1529 to 1543.

title: The Convention of Constantinople opens the Suez Canal to all
description: Nine powers, among them the United Kingdom, France and the Ottoman Empire, guaranteed free maritime passage through the canal in war and peace. The Khedivate of Egypt, through whose territory it ran, was not invited to the negotiations and did not sign.

title: The deposed Shuisky pays homage to Sigismund III in Warsaw
description: In the Senate Hall of the Royal Castle in Warsaw, Shuisky, deposed in Russia, and his retinue paid homage to King Sigismund III Vasa of Poland and the teenage Prince Władysław. Sigismund had moved his capital from Kraków to Warsaw.

title: John VI, a Greek from Ephesus, is elected pope
description: John VI was elected after the death of Sergius I on 8 September 701 and reigned during the Byzantine Papacy. His papacy was noted for military and political breakthroughs on the Italian Peninsula, and he died on 11 January 705.

title: Marinus II is elected pope during the Saeculum obscurum
description: Marinus II was elected after the death of Stephen VIII, whose pontificate had seen the power of popes diminished by the counts of Tusculum. Marinus was wrongly also called Martin III, so the second pope named Martin took the name Martin IV.

title: Hundreds of Muscogee die in the steamboat Monmouth disaster
description: About 311 Muscogee being forcibly removed to the Indian Territory died when the steamboat Monmouth collided at night on the Mississippi River above Baton Rouge. It was one of seven steamboats carrying roughly 3,000 Muscogee and enslaved Black people.

skip: A minor earthquake (at least two dead); trivial for a history site.

title: John Willis Menard becomes the first African American elected to Congress
description: Menard, a poet born in Kaskaskia, Illinois, to Louisiana Creole parents, was elected to the United States House of Representatives after moving to New Orleans. His opponent contested the result, and opposition kept him from being seated.

title: Paganino Doria captures the Venetian fleet at Sapienza
description: In the War of the Straits, the Genoese fleet under Paganino Doria defeated and captured the entire Venetian fleet of Niccolò Pisani in the Battle of Sapienza, also called Porto Longo. The war between the two maritime republics ended in 1355.

title: Forrest's cavalry strike the Union supply base at Johnsonville
description: Ending a 23-day raid through western Tennessee, Confederate cavalry under Nathan Bedford Forrest destroyed 28 Union boats and barges and millions of dollars of supplies at Johnsonville. It hampered George H. Thomas's plans against Hood's invasion of Tennessee.

title: Frederick the Great routs a French and Imperial army at Rossbach
description: In a 90-minute battle near Rossbach in the Electorate of Saxony, Frederick the Great's 22,000 Prussians defeated a French and Imperial army of 41,110 men. The battle was part of the Third Silesian War, within the Seven Years' War.

title: William McKinley is re-elected with Theodore Roosevelt
description: Republican President William McKinley defeated the Democrat William Jennings Bryan in a rematch of the 1896 election, with Governor Theodore Roosevelt of New York as his running mate. Roosevelt became president after McKinley's assassination in 1901.

skip: The first broadcast of a television programme (Meet the Press); a minor first for a history site.

title: Harrison's army fights Tecumseh's confederacy at Tippecanoe
description: Governor William Henry Harrison of the Indiana Territory marched about 1,000 men against Prophetstown, headquarters of the confederacy of Tecumseh and his brother Tenskwatawa. The battle at Battle Ground, Indiana, is often seen as the climax of Tecumseh's War.
